subject_matter.value: Painter Mark Rothko hires and spars with a young assistant, who reveals his parents' murder, challenges Rothko's views, and is fired and set free.
subject_matter.evidence: "I am your employer" and "You're fired."

literary_form.evidence: A cutting of a short story from a collection; the label "SGT PRICE:" was added.

tone.evidence: A flat soldier's voice recounts horrors: "We shot dogs. Not by accident."

content_warnings.evidence: He describes the torture house ("the body parts in the locker"), platoon deaths ("three members of your platoon died"), shooting his own dog, and post-war numbness ("I don't care if I die").

difficulty.evidence: One controlled voice whose numbness must carry the horror and the final killing.

audience_level.evidence: Torture, war deaths and the graphic shooting of a dog are described.

themes.evidence: "It'll be a long time before you get down to white" and "I'd been trained to do it right".

subject_matter.value: A Marine returning from Iraq describes his homecoming, his inability to relax, and putting down his old dog with his rifle.
subject_matter.evidence: "Getting back feels like your first breath" and "Two bullets tore through his chest".

literary_form.evidence: A cutting of a short story from a collection; the label "GRACE'S DAD" was added to the first-person narration.

tone.evidence: A father's gentle appeal for help hides something rotting in his car: "I didn't think cars could rot".

content_warnings.evidence: The father is coming apart ("It's hard now to recognize what's staring back") and the smell from the trunk he cannot open ("it's staring to smell") strongly implies his daughter's body.

difficulty.evidence: An unreliable narrator whose friendly surface must slowly reveal a horrifying subtext.

performance_demands.evidence: He addresses travellers and "holds out a flyer", and the reveal depends on slow, controlled delivery.

audience_level.evidence: The implied killing of a child and a father's breakdown are disturbing.

themes.evidence: "Now I can't remember which finger of mine touched her last" and "I can't leave until I find her".

subject_matter.value: A father living at a highway rest area hands out flyers about his missing daughter while hints reveal he lost his temper with her and her body may be in his car.
subject_matter.evidence: "Could you tell me if you've seen her?" and "I haven't been able to get into the trunk".

literary_form.evidence: A first-person narrative portrait from a book of New Testament sketches, with quoted dialogue and no speaker labels.

tone.evidence: A defiant prisoner ends in reverence: "I sink slowly to my knees."

content_warnings.evidence: Barabbas has watched crucifixions ("I have seen them die this slow") and describes Jesus on the cross among "the three dying men".

difficulty.evidence: One narrator with short quoted voices, moving from defiance to hope to awe.

audience_level.evidence: Crucifixion and suffering are described without graphic detail.

themes.evidence: "They are to crucify another in your place" and "the forgiveness of my crimes".

subject_matter.value: Barabbas waits in a dungeon for crucifixion, is freed in place of Jesus, and follows the crowd to Golgotha, where Jesus's look converts him.
subject_matter.evidence: "I am Barabbas" and "The place is called Golgotha".

literary_form.evidence: A cutting of a short story with narration shifting between persons; labels "RON:" and "SARAH:" were added.

tone.evidence: The narrator coolly examines his own cruelty: "I did not know how cruel this was."

content_warnings.evidence: "We made love that morning in my bed for long hours" and Sarah "drinks too much, until soon she is drunk".

difficulty.evidence: Two characters, deliberate shifts between first and third person, and a range from tenderness to cruelty.

performance_demands.evidence: Sarah's dialect-tinged speech ("Whatcha readin'") against Ron's narration, and a shift to anger in "Go on and leave".

audience_level.evidence: A sexual relationship, heavy drinking and profanity such as "son of a bitch" appear.

themes.evidence: "You're ashamed of being seen with me" and "I learned that I truly did love her".

subject_matter.value: A handsome man recalls his affair with a homely woman he met in a bar, his shame at being seen with her, his cruel rejection, and his late grief.
subject_matter.evidence: "Sarah was very homely" and "Go on and leave, you ugly bitch."

literary_form.evidence: A cutting of a parable from a collection of Gibran's writings; labels such as "SATAN:" and "NARRATOR:" were added.

tone.evidence: Satan mocks the priest's trade: "Do you not realize that you will starve to death if I were to die?"

content_warnings.evidence: Satan was beaten by angels ("struck me severely") and lies bleeding: "half of my blood has escaped".

difficulty.evidence: A very long argumentative speech with stories nested inside it, plus the priest and narrator.

performance_demands.evidence: Voices for SATAN, FATHER SAMAAN, the narrator, and quoted figures such as La Wiss and the Chief.

audience_level.evidence: A wounded figure and religious satire are present, with no graphic content.

themes.evidence: "I am the builder of convents and monasteries upon the foundation of fear."

subject_matter.value: A priest finds the wounded Satan, who argues that religion depends on him, and the priest carries him home to save his life.
subject_matter.evidence: "I am Satan." and "lifted Satan to his back and walked toward home".

literary_form.evidence: A cutting of a solo play spoken under the label "SCARAMOUCHE:" with stage directions.

tone.evidence: Clowning set against genocide: "the common euphemism for extermination" became "going to see the clown".

content_warnings.evidence: He digs mass graves as victims are "machine-gunned into the ground" in a concentration camp, and later sews his own mouth shut ("stitch the aperture with sutures").

difficulty.evidence: One character, but it demands a clown's mime alongside narration of atrocity.

performance_demands.evidence: Directions such as "performs the mime he used for the children" and "Performs one final" mime require silent physical work.

audience_level.evidence: Mass execution of children and adults is described directly.

value: Laughter in the face of death
themes.evidence: "I discovered a certain facility for making children laugh" and "I feel unmasked at last".

subject_matter.value: An ancient clown on the last night of his life tells how, as a camp gravedigger in World War II, he made children laugh before their execution and later sealed his lips for fifty years.
subject_matter.evidence: "a job as a gravedigger at the concentration camp" and "I never opened my mouth again".

tone.evidence: Boyhood games return as Dennis mourns: "Blood brothers."

performance_demands.evidence: Many voices (DENNIS, SCOOTER, EDDIE, MR. GREENBAUM) and business such as "Begins packing a suitcase" and throwing a ball.

themes.evidence: "I won't be made to feel responsible!" and "you didn't have to judge me".

themes.evidence: "Don't let them see you cry" and "The hurt had been too deep."

subject_matter.evidence: "I saw a sweet little girl who looked about fifteen, walking alone" and "the terrifying mob scenes at Central".

literary_form.evidence: A short story published in Boston Review, told in first-person narration with quoted dialogue.

tone.evidence: Magician's wit about "a shell game with organs" sits beside a dying mother and a dead parrot.

content_warnings.evidence: His parrot dies ("cradle his lifeless body in my arms") and his mother signals she wants to die: "Angry she doesn't have the strength, the means, to do it herself."

difficulty.evidence: A narrator with several short voices (Lois, mother, Sandkirk, the parrot) and shifts from comedy to grief.

performance_demands.evidence: The parrot's "Disappear! Disappear!", the mother's garbled speech and Lois must be voiced distinctly.

audience_level.evidence: A parent's wish to be killed is central, though nothing graphic occurs.

themes.evidence: "A magician pulling off a disappearing act" and "Not to kill her, but to be with her."
